📉 94,000 fewer payslips — and a Budget coming that wants more from you.

The numbers, not the adjectives:
• Payrolled employees down 94,000 on the year, to 30.3 million
• Unemployment 4.9% — 1.77 million people, up 88,000 in a year
• CPI inflation back up to 2.9% in July, from 2.6% in June
• Energy price cap up 4% to £1,723 from 1 October — about £60 a year more

🗓️ And on Wednesday 28 October, Andy Burnham's Chancellor delivers a Budget the PM has already hinted will raise taxes. He says he "won't be unrealistic" about the public finances. You don't need a decoder ring for that.

⚖️ Being straight with you: 4.9% unemployment isn't 1981, and some of the gas price pressure really is global. But every indicator is pointing the wrong way at once, and has been for months. That's not weather — that's climate.

🔨 You don't tax your way out of a jobs problem. Make hiring cheaper, make work pay, and get the levies off energy bills.
